import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 19

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/



namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 19](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

If `G` is connected then the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies
`b(G) ≥ FLOOR((∑ ecc(v))/(|V|) + sSup (range (l G)))`, where `ecc(v)` denotes
eccentricity and `l(G)` is the independence number of neighbourhoods.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture19 (G : SimpleGraph α) [Nontrivial α] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    ⌊(∑ v ∈ Finset.univ, ((G.eccent v).toNat : ℝ)) / (Fintype.card α : ℝ) +
      sSup (Set.range (indepNeighbors G))⌋ ≤ b G := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19

reformulations.difference: Lean additionally assumes `Nontrivial α`; the source states the conjecture for simple connected graphs without explicitly excluding the one-vertex graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only omitted connected finite graph is K₁. Its eccentricity and neighborhood independence number are both zero, so the proposed lower bound is zero and the inequality holds (its bipartite number is one). Thus restricting to graphs with at least two vertices is equivalent to the unrestricted connected-graph statement. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/reformulations.lean without using the conjecture.

reformulations.difference: The source uses finite maxima and ordinary eccentricities; Lean uses a real supremum for local independence and converts extended-natural eccentricity with `.toNat`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The neighborhood-independence range is finite and nonempty, so its real supremum is its attained maximum. In a finite connected graph all distances are finite and eccentricity is an attained finite maximum, so `.toNat` preserves its value. A direct equivalence with the formulation using finite natural-number maxima was proved in /workspace/review/source_equivalence.lean.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II: authoritative JavaScript listing, conjecture entry 19 and definitions 4, 5, 15, 21, and 22: https://web.archive.org/web/20240726225301id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowii/wowIIdefs.js
D. B. West, Some Conjectures of Graffiti.pc (2004–07), definitions and references: https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/regs/graffiti.html
Jingru Yan, Estimating the circumference of a graph in terms of its leaf number, abstract inspected while locating references: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02653
